clue.text: Assign a parking place

parts.note: P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
a point is a particular place or spot

explanation.surface: Someone allocates a motorist a parking spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'a parking place' reads as what is assigned, but it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To appoint someone is to nominate or allot them to a role.

clue.text: Old article covering new things to be done

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the outer pieces surround the abbreviation for new

parts.note: aged means old
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An ancient piece of writing deals with new items requiring action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts AGED+A around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items for action, especially at a meeting, is the plural Latin for tasks to be carried out.

clue.text: One providing initial painkiller and care amid disaster?

definitions.text: One providing initial painkiller and care amid disaster?

indicators.note: initial means the opening letter of the following word
a disaster is a mess or wreck, signalling that the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A medic arrives at an emergency to give first pain relief and attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' gives P from painkiller; 'disaster' rearranges CAREAMID into ARAMEDIC. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance crew member gives emergency treatment at accident scenes before hospital.

clue.text: You have to be left in their organisation

indicators.note: organisation here means arranging, so the letters of the two words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: You must bequeath something in the way their institution works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges INTHEIR. The definition reads as a cryptic sense: what you get when something is left to you in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into property by bequest is to receive what has been willed to you.

clue.text: Appropriated money, say, in bags

explanation.surface: Pocketing cash while wearing loose trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bags is British slang for loose trousers, so 'in bags' means wearing trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for pocketing cash, and also describing someone wearing pairs of slacks.

clue.text: Food shared out, a proportion going to partners

parts.note: a ratio is a proportion between two quantities
N and S, North and South, are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Food is divided up, with a share going to each couple.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S are bridge partners (North and South), a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Rations are fixed allowances of provisions distributed to each person.

clue.text: Twinned city father

parts.note: a city father who was himself one of twins: one of the legendary pair of brothers suckled by a wolf, who founded Rome

explanation.surface: An official from a town that has a twin town abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twinned city' suggests town twinning; it means a founding father who was a twin.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the twin brother of Romulus helped found Rome.

clue.text: Thin cloth put over rich cheese

indicators.note: put over in a down clue means turned upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: fat means rich, as of food
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: A fine fabric is laid on top of a creamy cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put over' reverses FAT to TAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, fine silk or synthetic fabric.

clue.text: Old goat initially went ahead and gave a lewd look

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of the word that precedes it

parts.note: led means went ahead, in front

explanation.surface: An old lecher went first and leered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old goat' reads as a lecherous man, but it splits into O and the first letter of goat.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone with lustful interest.

clue.text: Seaman's leader exhausting bad language

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word next to it

parts.note: wearing means tiring or exhausting

explanation.surface: A sailor's chief is worn out by foul talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursing and profanity are both kinds of offensive speech.

clue.text: Grotesque marrow the underground worker produced

indicators.note: grotesque means distorted out of shape, so the letters of the two words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A misshapen vegetable gives rise to a creature of the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing invertebrate toils beneath the soil, aerating it, hence a worker below ground.

clue.text: Fictitious invalid

explanation.surface: An illness that was only made up.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something untrue: made up, or not holding good.

clue.text: Dissent, mostly decorous

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: demure means modest and decorous

explanation.surface: A polite, restrained objection.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection, the verb form of disagreeing.

clue.text: Dress up last pair of firemen specially — one supports hose

indicators.note: specially here means arranged in a special way, signalling that the letters are rearranged
the last pair of a word is its final two letters, here taken from firemen

explanation.surface: Firefighters dress up in a special way, with something holding up a hose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last pair of' takes EN from firemen; with DRESSUP these letters are rearranged. 'Hose' suggests the fire hose but means stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is a strap that holds up a stocking, and hose are stockings.

clue.text: Discourage speaking about current slump

indicators.note: about here means set around, so the two words are placed around the letter for current

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
oration is formal public speaking
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Discouraging talk about the present leads to a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DETERORATION around I, so the I sits between the two pieces. 'Current' looks like 'present' but is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A slump is a decline or worsening, a falling off in condition.

clue.text: Bound by contract to big deal as arranged

indicators.note: as arranged signals that the letters of the preceding words are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Committed by agreement to a large transaction as planned.
explanation.definitionFit: Being legally bound to do something means having a duty to do it.

clue.text: Senior officer batting first, usually

indicators.note: first says the batting piece comes before the officer

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is said to be in
a general is a high-ranking army officer

explanation.surface: A high-ranking officer normally goes in to bat first.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side currently batting is said to be 'in'; 'first' is an indicator placing that piece ahead of the officer.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means as a rule, on the whole.

clue.text: Sailors surrounded by the drink

parts.note: ABs, able seamen, are sailors
in means surrounded by, enclosed in

explanation.surface: Seamen are caught up in drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' looks like a container signal but here simply supplies a word meaning enclosed; the drink is read literally piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed-flavoured spirit.

clue.text: Reversing previous approach, support promotion, say

parts.note: to back something is to support it

indicators.note: say signals that a word is to be heard rather than spelt, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: peddling is promoting or pushing goods or ideas

explanation.surface: A change of policy is presented as support for advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives the sound of PEDDLING spelt as PEDALLING, as on a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpedal is to retreat from an earlier stated position.

clue.text: Inspector for each employer

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
a user is one who employs something

explanation.surface: A checker for each company boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employer' suggests a boss but means one who uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who peruses reads or examines a text carefully.

clue.text: Switching sections, enters lots of money received

indicators.note: switching sections means the two parts of the phrase trade places

parts.note: comes in means enters

explanation.surface: Moving between departments brings big earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switching sections' swaps COMES IN to IN COMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings, the money people take in, are their revenue.

clue.text: Heartless boy grabbing composer in noisy argument

indicators.note: grabbing means holding inside, so the composer goes within
heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: taken as written
Thomas Arne was an English composer, of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A cruel lad seizes a musician in a loud quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' leaves BY, and 'grabbing' wraps that round the composer. Arne is a crossword favourite among composers.
explanation.definitionFit: Barney is British slang for a loud quarrel or row.

clue.text: Carrying out confinement at home and coming round, we hear

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: we hear signals that the next word is given by its sound

parts.note: turning is coming round, as a corner or a tide

explanation.surface: Someone is housebound and recovering consciousness, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns TURNING into its sound-alike TERNING. 'Confinement' suggests childbirth but means detention.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern people is to detain them, especially in wartime, so this is imposing detention.

clue.text: Taking a minute, unruly youth's broken in

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so the youth goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a Ted, a Teddy boy, was an unruly 1950s British youth

explanation.surface: After a minute, a wild youngster has been subdued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' puts TED around A and M. 'Broken in' reads as burgled but means trained.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is broken in has been trained and made docile.

clue.text: New copper is about to get a hearing aid

indicators.note: about here means around, so the two letters sit within the outer pair

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A rookie policeman is about to be given a deaf aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal. The definition is witty: the bone helps you hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The incus is one of the small bones of the middle ear that pass sound along.

clue.text: Line dance

explanation.surface: A dance where the participants form a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin American dance is performed in a long single-file chain, which is also called by its name.

clue.text: Turned over piece of semi-transparent paper

indicators.note: turned over signals the letters are read in the opposite direction
piece of signals a run of letters taken from inside the next words

explanation.surface: A sheet of tracing paper flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of' takes SEMIT from semi-transparent, and 'Turned over' reverses it. The Times is a London newspaper, so the clue names itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times is a national newspaper, and a paper is a newspaper.

clue.text: One vessel or another crossing a river

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the second vessel goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a can is another kind of vessel, a container
the Tamar is a river in south-west England, between Devon and Cornwall

explanation.surface: A boat or some other craft fords a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' wraps the second vessel round the river and the A. 'Vessel' first suggests a ship, but the second one is a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a twin-hulled boat, a type of seagoing craft.

clue.text: Sticks seen in brooks

explanation.surface: Twigs spotted floating in streams.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick it out and to brook something both mean to put up with or tolerate it.

clue.text: Girl turned out for pageant

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
to splay is to spread or turn outwards

explanation.surface: A young woman shows up for a beauty contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a spectacle or show put on for public viewing.
